machine: Windows amd64, Intel Core i7-9750H, 1920x1080 synthetic RGBA frames
method: Five iterations per case in one process, comparing the previous pooled standard-library BestSpeed PNG encoder against the sampled Sub/Up encoder on the same deterministic source frame. Only synthetic document, mixed document/noise and random-noise pixels were used. No desktop images were saved.
interpretation: The paired mixed-content PNG case used about 75% less encoding time with effectively the same file size. Document PNG encoding used about 51% less time with 103 additional bytes. Adaptive capture still selects uncompressed PNG for random noise. These short runs took place on a loaded development machine; they do not establish end-to-end hotkey latency, screen-driver timing or a universal speedup. Both encoders preserve source pixels; standard PNG decoding verifies CRCs and zlib streams in regression tests.
memory_and_cancellation: Pooled compressors and chunk buffers reset their writers to io.Discard after every encode, releasing the original frame and output-buffer references
Generic/transparent/16-bit images use the standard encoder without pooling its source-retaining EncoderBuffer
Capture encoding checks cancellation between groups of 16 rows and discards partial output
Compression probes read RGBA pixels directly instead of boxing 8192 sampled colors and count compressed bytes without storing another buffer
